chunks: And from him, from Safwan, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked one of the two Imams (peace be upon them both) about a man who performed Tawaf around the House (Kaaba) but became exhausted; should he delay the Sa'i (walking) between al-Safa and al-Marwah? He said, 'Yes.'
And as for what we mentioned regarding the ruling that it is not permissible to delay it until the next day, that has been narrated.

key_terms.الصَّفَا: al-Safa (one of the hills in Mecca)

ai.seo_question: Can a pilgrim delay Sa'i between Safa and Marwah if they are too tired after Tawaf?
ai.summary: In this narration from Sahih al-Tusi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) permits a pilgrim exhausted after Tawaf to defer Sa'i to the following day, illustrating the principle of *rukhas* (concessions) in Shia fiqh when physical hardship arises. While some jurists restrict such delays to the immediate ritual window, this hadith highlights the flexibility granted to ensure the completion of Hajj pillars without undue burden, a key distinction in Usuli interpretations of ritual validity.
